title: POC sprint runway — proposal and workshop notebook
content:
Goal / one-liner:
Deliver a tightly-scoped 3-week POC that proves: predictable latency at 99th pct SLA, <30% cost delta with suggested batching/quantization, and no functional regression on customer prompt-suite.

Background / context:
- Prospect: FinReg Insights (data-sensitive financial analytics). Must run inference within customer VPC (private deployment) OR use Dedicated with strict data isolation.
- Customer priority: latency on short queries (average 16 tokens) + secure ingestion pipeline.
- Current ask: 3-week proof that our hosted runtime can meet latency targets and provide cost projections for scale.

Top success criteria (S.M.A.R.T):
1) 99th percentile token latency <= 120ms for the primary prompt profile (avg input length 16 tokens) during sustained 50 RPS for 10m windows.
2) End-to-end throughput baseline forecast within +/- 15% of measured pilot.
3) Evaluation pass rate >= 95% on customer prompt set (syntactic correctness + domain accuracy checklist).
4) Deployment runbook and rollback tested with one simulated region outage.

Non-goals (avoid scope creep):
- Model training/fine-tuning is out of scope.
- Long-tail prompt coverage and stress tests beyond 200 RPS not in this pilot.

Proposed timeline (3-week runway) — high level:
Week 0 (pre-onramp, 3 business days) — alignment and infra prep
- Kickoff + security review (customer + infra) — owners: Asha, Liam
- Collect prompt-suite + golden responses from customer (data transfer checklist) — owner: Maya
- Provision Dedicated pool (or VPC private endpoint) with 2 GPUs — owner: Diego 

Week 1 — workshop + baseline run
- Day 1: Onsite/remote workshop (2 hrs): architecture review, SLOs, measurement plan, and test harness walkthrough. Agenda below.
- Day 2–5: Baseline runs using unoptimized model: measure latency distribution, cold-start characteristics, KV cache warmup profile. Owners: eng SRE + solutions eng.

Week 2 — optimizations and targeted experiments
- Apply batching and prefix cache settings; try INT8 quantization candidate for cost test.
- Run A/B with fallback model variant (smaller model) to validate graceful degradation.
- Collect quality metrics on prompt-suite and log divergence rate.

Week 3 — runbook, wrap-up, and exec demo
- Conduct failure injection (region outage, GPU preemption) and validate automatic fallback.
- Final cost/latency deck and recommended config for production.
- Customer exec demo + decision review.

Workshop Day 1 detailed agenda (90–120 min):
- 00–10m: Introductions, objectives, and acceptance criteria (Asha)
- 10–30m: Architecture walkthrough: on-prem vs Dedicated decision tree (Liam)
- 30–50m: Measurement plan: metrics, dashboards, logs to collect (Maya)
- 50–80m: Hands-on test harness & local run example (Diego)
- 80–90m: Risk register and contingency playbook (group)
- 90–120m: Q&A + action item capture

Action item tracker (short form — expand in Jira):
- POC-1: Share sanitized prompt-suite + golden set — owner: Customer; due: 2024-09-16 — status: pending
- POC-2: Provision Dedicated pool 2xA10G (or 1xH100 alt) — owner: Diego; due: 2024-09-17 — status: in_progress
- POC-3: Create test harness repo + CI job to run perf sweep — owner: Maya; due: 2024-09-18 — status: in_progress
- POC-4: Security review (network, KMS, audit logging) — owner: Liam; due: 2024-09-19 — status: planned
- POC-5: Run baseline 8-hour soak and collect metrics — owner: SRE; due: 2024-09-24 — status: planned

Measurement plan (key signals):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for token generation and end-to-end request
- Cost: $/1k tokens for observed batching profile, plus projected monthly cost at target volume
- Quality: pass/fail on domain checklist per prompt + semantic similarity delta to golden responses
- Reliability: error rate, fallback invocation rate, and time-to-failover

Quick risk heatmap (mitigations):
- Data transfer restrictions — Mitigation: use customer SFTP + ephemeral storage; confirm KMS policy pre-kickoff
- SLA miss under burst — Mitigation: autoscale burst config with reserve capacity; pre-stage warm caches
- Quality regression from quantization — Mitigation: gated experiment with human-in-loop checks; fallback to FP16 variant

Runbook excerpts / checklists (to test during final week):
- Deploy change to staging pool; run synthetic 30m sweep at 50 RPS; validate p99 < 120ms
- Simulate region failure: cut traffic to primary region, validate failover within 60s and no session loss >1%
- Revoke token/key rotation: verify new keys accepted and old tokens rejected per policy

Notes-to-self / open questions: (raw)
- Will customer accept temporary access to audit logs? need legal signoff (escalate to security).
- Consider running a micro-benchmark that isolates KV cache effect separately (short vs long prefix).
- If Dedicated GPUs are delayed, fallback plan: use hosted with VPC peering + contract clause for data residency.

Customer deliverables at close:
- Config snapshot (model version + runtime flags)
- Perf deck (latency, throughput graphs, cost forecast)
- Runbook + rollback playbook (shared, editable)
- Recommendation: production capacity and recommended SLAs

Communications cadence:
- Daily 15m standup during active weeks (internal) — owner: Asha
- Twice-weekly customer sync (Tue/Thu 30m) — owner: Maya
- Slack channel: #poc-finsight-runway (invite: eng-sre, sec, prod)

Appendix: quick experiment matrix (to run in Week 2)
- E1: Batch sizes 1,4,8 with continuous batching window 20ms — measure p99 and token cost
- E2: Prefix KV enabled vs disabled — measure cold-start penalty and avg latency
- E3: INT8 quantization candidate on smaller model — measure quality delta and cost reduction
- E4: Fallback routing to lighter model under saturation — validate response continuity and quality threshold

Reference links (internal):
- Perf harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-scripts
- Runbook template: confluence://templates/poc-runbook
- Related Jira epic: JIRA-POC-3432

End of notebook.

- Confirm Maya has the golden prompt-set by EOD Friday
- Ping legal re: audit-log access (Liam)
